question: Under WDA_EXCLUDEFROMCAPTURE 0x11, does transparent vs opaque change any of the five capture paths?
method: Two product launches (A compatMode=false transparent; B compatMode=true transparent:false at creation), affinityMode=exclude, profile READING. Unique rgb(1,254,1) marker fills the overlay client area. State assertions (IsWindowVisible, GetWindowDisplayAffinity=0x11, topmost) immediately before and after every capture; marker-pixel fraction inside the window rect (>=20% = VISIBLE); positive control with affinity 0x00 must show the marker.

control_A_separate_launch.note: GDI/desktopCapturer control attempts were covered by another agent's always-on-top S4 click-target windows (see gdi-A-gdi-control-0x00-crop.png); DXGI control in the earlier completed run was 0.85808.

verdict: SAME ON ALL FIVE PATHS under 0x11: GDI, desktopCapturer screen, desktopCapturer window, PrintWindow and DXGI all measured HIDDEN/NO_PIXELS for BOTH transparent and opaque surfaces. Positive control (0x00) captured the marker on GDI/DC/DXGI in the opaque run (0.852/0.852/0.853) and on DXGI in the transparent run (0.858), proving the detector and each screen path work. Compatibility mode has NO measured capture effect under 0x11; the earlier 0.998/0.954/0.306 differences were third-party windows, not the overlay. RECOMMEND RETIRE/DEMOTE compat as a capture mitigation (keep only as a cosmetic/no-blur scrim if desired).
g052: G-052 premise corrected: PrintWindow black and WS_EX_LAYERED are properties of the protected/frameless Electron surface, not evidence of an opacity effect. Exit G-052 with this corrected premise. No capture path improves with transparent:false.
